text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: autoscale-throttle (prod, us-west-2) fired at 2026-03-15T03:40:00Z. tokens_per_sec spiked to 610k, queue_depth climbed to ~720, throttle_events increased to 18/min. Pager routed to #eng-oncall. Related customer-facing 429s observed in apiv2 cluster.

maria: ack-ing, i'm on it. pulling up dashboards and recent deploys. any active rollouts?

aj: no rolls in the last 2 hours from my side. saw a batch job completing slowly in analytics that could be sending longer prompts.

sam: just saw the same. apiv2 latency p95 jumped from 120ms -> 1.2s in last 7m. requests/tokens spike looks correlated with a small client sending long sequences.

lee: quick mitigation options: 1) bump dedicated pool by +2 pods (fast but might take 2-4m), 2) enable burst-capacity policy for apiv2 (instant if enabled), 3) route a portion of traffic to smaller model to reduce tokens/sec.

maria: let's do 2 then 1. aj please flip burst policy toggle, sam can you open a temporary routing rule to divert 15% to model-small? i'll notify ops to pre-warm nodes.

aj: toggling burst-capacity now -> 'ON' (ui), applying policy id `burst-apiv2-2026-03`.

incidents-bot: action executed: burst-capacity enabled for apiv2. autoscaler note: short-term CPU headroom allowed.

sam: adding a quick traffic rule:```
# temporary weighted routing
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $API" 
  https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/route/update 
  -d '{"route":"/v2/generate","weights":{"model-small":15,"model-large":85}}'
```

devon: pre-warming 2 nodes in the dedicated pool (g5x) now, ETA ~3m. watching schedule.

maria: after burst + routing, tokens/sec dropped to ~240k and queue_depth down to 180 in 4m. throttle_events -> 2/min. early win. customers still seeing intermittent 429s, but reduced.

aj: note for follow-up: current alert threshold is tokens_per_sec > 500k for 3m with no debounce. that caused an immediate page. suggest changing to 2-stage alerts: warning at 350k (5m) and page at 600k (2m) but require throttle_rate > 5/min for paging.

sam: also propose smarter rule for queue_depth: page when queue_depth > 600 AND tokens/sec per pod > 10k (to avoid noisy spikes).

lee: agree. will add a dashboard panel showing tokens/sec per model, tokens/sec per pod, and throttle_events/1m ratio. that'll help triage quickly.

maria: log actions/timeline in the incident runbook and create a short post-incident task list. immediate items: (1) adjust alert debounce and add throttle-rate gating, (2) create per-model tokens/sec panel, (3) add runbook step to flip burst-capacity and temp-route, (4) investigate upstream client sending long prompts.

incidents-bot: Incident status updated -> mitigated. Severity: S2 -> monitoring. Open tasks created: #INC-4321 (alert-tuning), #INC-4322 (dashboards), #INC-4323 (client-investigation).

devon: capturing the autoscaler config change we made in case we need to roll back:```
autoscaler:
  name: apiv2-autoscaler
  burst_enabled: true
  burst_max_nodes: 5
  scale_up_delay: 30s
  scale_down_delay: 2m
```

aj: follow-up notes: change paging policy to require throttle_events >= 5/min within window when tokens/sec > 500k, and add a 90s debounce on high-frequency spikes. I'll file an alert PR.

maria: thanks all. i'll do the customer comms summary and loop in success for impacted tenants. leave any logs/screenshots in the incident doc. :thumbsup:

lee: one more thing — adding a correlation metric: throttles_per_100k_tokens to detect efficiency regressions. adding to dashboards.

sam: last_message: will monitor for 30m and then close the slack thread if stable.
